title: Parallel eval paths and timeout hardening for relevancy-evaluator
creator: Asha Natarajan
description: Goal: Reduce 95th/99th percentile latency for the relevancy-evaluator endpoint while keeping end-to-end score quality loss <= 1.5% on baseline datasets. Scope covers request-side microbatching, parallel evaluation lanes (fast/approximate + slow/high-quality), per-request token enforcement, and robust soft/hard timeout behavior with graceful fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency for 512-token candidate sets reduced by 25% versus current canary on staging under representative QPS
End-to-end rerank quality regression <= 1.5% measured on dev-eval prompt set (NDCG@10 and pairwise accuracy)
No increased error-rate in hosted tier beyond 0.2% during week-long canary at 10% traffic
New metrics emitted: lane_accept_rate, lane_latency_{fast,slow}, token_truncated_count, soft_timeout_rate, hard_timeout_rate
Automated rollback trigger defined if hard_timeout_rate > 0.5% or client_error_rate increases > 0.3%
technical_design: Introduce two parallel evaluation lanes inside the endpoint: "express" lane uses a 4-bit quantized model variant with aggressive KV cache reuse and 12-token generation cap; "thorough" lane uses float16 model with full-context scoring and higher token budget.

Scheduler: on request arrival, try to build a candidate microbatch and place into express lane; if express batch is full/oversubscribed or candidate set flagged 'high-quality' by heuristic, route to thorough lane or duplicate to both lanes for hedging.
Token limits: enforce per-candidate and per-request token ceilings at the runtime boundary; if a candidate exceeds the cap, apply truncation policy with metadata warning (token_truncated_count).

Timeouts: soft timeout (e.g., 120ms per microbatch) triggers fallback to express lane partial results; hard timeout (e.g., 300ms) cancels in-flight work and returns best-effort result with telemetry. Both timeouts configurable via route-level policy and dynamic flags.
Batching: continuous batching with max_latency=25ms and dynamic batch size cap based on recent p95 latency signal; allow speculative early dispatch when priority header is set.
KV cache coordination: express lane aggressively reuses prefix KV when requests share embedding keys; implement conservative cache invalidation to avoid staleness for model variants.
Observability: emit per-request tags for lane_taken, lane_success, truncated_tokens, and timeout_phase. Add traces that link to GPU kernel selection and batch composition.
Fallthrough: if express lane returns but quality score below threshold, trigger background re-eval on thorough lane and patch results via subsequent client websocket push (best-effort).
rollout_plan: Week 0: Unit + integration tests, local microbench harness. PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/4567
Week 1: Internal canary on staging (5% traffic) with synthetic load that matches production token distribution. Monitor lane_accept_rate and soft/hard timeouts.
Week 2: Expand to 10% production traffic gated by: p95 latency improvement achieved AND hard_timeout_rate < 0.2% for 48h.
Week 3: 50% traffic if weekly quality regression <= 1.5% on eval harness; otherwise iterate on thresholds and batching params.
Rollback: immediate rollback to previous runtime variant if hard_timeout_rate > 0.5% or client visible error increase > 0.3% over baseline within 1h.
Post-rollout: run 2-week A/B quality analysis and collect cost delta report.
implementation_notes: Spike results: local bench with 4xV100-equivalent nodes shows 22% p95 improvement for candidate sets of size 128 using express lane + microbatching (bench id spike-2026-02-28)
Estimated cost impact: +8% GPU cycles for thorough lane hedging, but expected net token cost reduction of 12% due to prefix cache reuse and fewer end-to-end retries

Key PRs: runtime patch (github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/4567), api adapter (github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-api/pull/788), console telemetry (github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1122)
Schema changes: add lane_tag string to request metadata and new telemetry metrics; migration is read-only for older clients.
QA: fuzz tests for token truncation edge cases, e2e tests that compare express vs thorough output quality for 1k canonical prompts.
